factProposals.value: A map in the staff console plotting every work order at its coordinates, with the heat map as a layer, filtered by date range, status and work type; work orders without coordinates are listed beside it with the reason.
City planners (and supervisors and administrators) see the heat map layer; anyone who can read work orders sees the plotted points.
The map checks each plotted work order's linked asset against GIS through the existing GIS client and flags any difference from the stored record.
When GIS does not answer, the map says so and still shows every work order from its stored record; a date range with no work orders is shown as empty, not as an error.
factProposals.evidence: tests/mapView.test.js (GIS times out; a date range with no work orders)

factProposals.value: No street basemap is shown: a basemap needs an outside map service that the city has not provided, and the console only loads content from its own server.

decisions.statement: Place work orders on the map with the heat map's own rule and filters.
decisions.rationale: The map and the heat map must never disagree about which work orders are where.
decisions.evidence: server/mapView.js (mapPoints uses normaliseParams); tests/mapView.test.js (always count the same work orders)

decisions.statement: Have the console draw exactly what the map endpoint returns, never computing positions itself.
decisions.rationale: What is displayed and what is stored cannot disagree.
decisions.evidence: server/api/consoleRoutes.js (/console/map); tests/mapView.test.js (returns exactly what mapPoints gives)

decisions.statement: Flag a GIS difference rather than move the point.
decisions.rationale: The stored record is what the rest of the system uses; the GIS sync resolves the difference, and the map shows both positions until it does.

decisions.statement: Draw the map on a coordinate grid without a street layer.
decisions.rationale: A basemap needs an outside map service and account the city has not provided; the city's own GIS can show the same data as GeoJSON.

limitations.statement: There is no street basemap, and GIS assets are not shown as reference points because the GIS client fetches assets by id and cannot list them.
Work orders entered with a freeform location only cannot be placed on the map.
At most 5,000 work orders are plotted at once.
